AssisT TTS Highlight Test Fixture

Open this file in Chrome with the AssisT extension loaded. Open the popup, enable TTS, turn on Word-by-Word, then click each test paragraph to verify the expected behaviour.

Case 1 — basic paragraph

The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog beside the ancient oak tree by the river.

Expected: each word lights up as it is spoken; sync should be tight on local voices, slightly looser on Google network voices but still finish near the end of speech.

Case 2 — paragraph containing a link (regression check)

This paragraph contains an important inline link that the user might want to click after reading.

Expected: the link stays visible and clickable during reading. After cleanup, click the link — it should navigate. Pre-PR behavior destroyed the link during reading.

Case 3 — paragraph containing a button (regression check)

Read this paragraph, then click the to confirm its event handler survived word-wrapping.

Expected: button click triggers the alert. Pre-PR behavior would have destroyed the button.

Case 4 — paragraph with bold and italic inline formatting

This paragraph has bold words and italic words that should remain styled while the highlight passes through them.

Expected: bold/italic styles remain visible during reading (text-node walker preserves inline elements). Pre-PR behavior wiped formatting.

Case 5 — paragraph with embedded contenteditable

Read this paragraph but do not wrap me, I am editable so the highlight should skip me.

Expected: words outside the editable span get highlighted. Words inside (yellow background) are NOT wrapped and remain editable. Try clicking and typing in the yellow span — should work.

Case 6 — heading element (h2 itself)

A standalone heading element with sufficient text length to be read by TTS.

Expected: clicking on this heading reads the heading itself with word-by-word highlight.

Case 7 — list items

  1. First list item with several words for the highlight tracker.
  2. Second list item with several words for the highlight tracker.
  3. Third list item with several words for the highlight tracker.
Expected (paragraph mode): clicking each list item reads only that item. Expected (section mode): clicking any list item reads the whole article (depending on ancestor).

Case 8 — blockquote with nested paragraph (leafmost regression check)

This paragraph is nested inside a blockquote element which is also a text-leaf.

Expected: in section/page mode, the nested <p> is wrapped (NOT the <blockquote>), so we don't get double-wrapping. Verify with DevTools that only one set of .assist-word spans appears during reading.

Case 9 — div with direct text (no nested paragraphs)

This is a plain div that contains only text and no nested block elements at all.
Expected: clicking reads the div's full text in word-by-word. (Without the leaf-fallback fix, this case would do nothing.)

Case 10 — div mixing direct text and nested paragraphs

Intro text right here.

Then a nested paragraph follows the intro.

Expected (paragraph mode): clicking reads ALL of div content, including both "Intro text right here" AND "Then a nested paragraph follows the intro" (paragraph mode treats target as one leaf).

Case 11 — long paragraph for autoscroll (page mode test)

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua.

Ut enim ad minim veniam, quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris nisi ut aliquip ex ea commodo consequat.

Duis aute irure dolor in reprehenderit in voluptate velit esse cillum dolore eu fugiat nulla pariatur.

Excepteur sint occaecat cupidatat non proident, sunt in culpa qui officia deserunt mollit anim id est laborum.

Sed ut perspiciatis unde omnis iste natus error sit voluptatem accusantium doloremque laudantium.

Totam rem aperiam, eaque ipsa quae ab illo inventore veritatis et quasi architecto beatae vitae dicta sunt explicabo.

Nemo enim ipsam voluptatem quia voluptas sit aspernatur aut odit aut fugit, sed quia consequuntur magni dolores.

Eos qui ratione voluptatem sequi nesciunt. Neque porro quisquam est, qui dolorem ipsum quia dolor sit amet.

Consectetur, adipisci velit, sed quia non numquam eius modi tempora incidunt ut labore et dolore magnam aliquam.

Expected (page mode + word-by-word): switch to "Whole page" in popup, click any paragraph here. The page should scroll smoothly to keep the active word in view as it advances. Press Space to pause; scrolling should freeze. Press Space again; scrolling and highlight resume from the same word.

Case 12 — script tag (defensive parser check)

Before the script. After the script.

Expected: script content is NOT wrapped in word-spans (would break execution). Walker should skip text inside <script>. Verify with DevTools that the script element's children are unchanged during reading.

Case 13 — quick double-click (race check)

First test paragraph for the rapid double-click race-condition stress test.

Second test paragraph for the rapid double-click race-condition stress test.

Expected: click case13a, then immediately (within 100ms) click case13b. Reading switches cleanly to case13b with no orphan spans left in case13a's DOM. Inspect both paragraphs after — neither should have any .assist-word remnants.

Case 14 — pause/resume test

A long paragraph for testing pause and resume behaviour without the highlight getting out of sync after a pause-resume cycle which is the most common bug class.

Expected: click to start. After ~3 words, press Space (pause). Wait 5 seconds. Press Space again (resume). The highlight should resume from the SAME word, not a different one, and stay aligned with subsequent speech.
